message: Select a Mountain or Plains card
annotation_description: Fetched Sacred Foundry (paying 2 additional life to have it enter untapped) when a basic Plains would have entered untapped for free. They already have a Sacred Foundry in hand for future red mana needs, plus Sunbaked Canyon. The unnecessary 2 life loss is meaningful against a UB deck that can pressure life totals.

Fetched Watery Grave when they already had one in hand, paying an unnecessary 2 life (from shock) against an aggressive equipment deck with Leyline Axe. A basic Swamp would provide BB for Emperor of Bones or Sign in Blood on turn 2, then play the Watery Grave from hand turn 3 for Psychic Frog.

The player should have played Arid Mesa from hand as their land for the turn before casting Stoneforge Mystic. Playing the land first costs nothing and preserves options (e.g., later sacrificing Sunbaked Canyon to draw a card if mana is available from Arid Mesa instead).

Casting Sign in Blood before playing Polluted Delta from hand. Should play the land first to preserve options after seeing the two drawn cards - they might draw something they want to deploy this turn with the extra mana from the fetch land.

Stoneforge Mystic's activated ability costs {1}{W} and tap. The player has Sacred Foundry (W/R) and Sunbaked Canyon (W/R) untapped, plus Paradise Mantle is on the battlefield (but not equipped to anything that can tap). Actually, looking more carefully: Sacred Foundry can produce W, Sunbaked Canyon can produce W or R (pay 1 life), and Urza's Saga on chapter II can produce C. So the player has access to {C}{W}{W/R} = 3 mana. Stoneforge Mystic costs {1}{W} to activate, which is easily payable. The player could activate Stoneforge Mystic to put Colossus Hammer directly onto the battlefield from hand, bypassing its {8} equip cost (they'd still need to equip it later, but getting it onto the battlefield is important for Urza's Saga construct tokens and for future Stoneforge/equip lines). This is a free equipment cheat that the player declined for no good reason.

The player has an Arid Mesa in hand and a land drop available (they haven't played a land this turn). Playing Arid Mesa would give them access to additional mana next turn and also trigger Revolt for potential Fatal Push synergies in the future. Missing a land drop when you have a land in hand is almost always wrong, especially when Stoneforge Mystic needs mana to activate (putting equipment onto the battlefield costs 1W) and equipping Leyline Axe costs 3. The player needs mana to execute their game plan of getting Colossus Hammer or Leyline Axe equipped.

Cracking Arid Mesa to fetch a Sacred Foundry when they already have a Sacred Foundry in hand they could play as their land drop. This wastes 1 life (plus potentially 2 more for untapped) unnecessarily, and loses the fetch land which could be saved for later turns when revolt might matter or when they need to thin the deck at a better time.

Stoneforge Mystic has an activated ability ({1}{W}, {T}: Put an Equipment card from your hand onto the battlefield) that could put one of the two Leyline Axes from hand directly onto the battlefield. The player has Sacred Foundry (untapped) + Sunbaked Canyon (untapped) available to pay {1}{W}, and Stoneforge Mystic is untapped. Cheating a Leyline Axe into play would give the option to equip it to a creature (or have it ready), and more importantly it's a free equipment drop that increases Construct token size from Urza's Saga. Passing without using Stoneforge Mystic's ability wastes a key tempo advantage - especially since Stoneforge could tap to put Leyline Axe into play before combat, and the player could still play the Sacred Foundry from hand for other uses later.

Attacking with Stoneforge Mystic taps it, preventing use of its activated ability ({1}{W}, {T}) to put a Leyline Axe from hand onto the battlefield this turn. The attack risks the Mystic dying to a 2/2 Emperor of Bones block for at most 1 damage, while the Mystic's ability to cheat in equipment is far more valuable. With Colossus Hammer and Leyline Axe available, keeping Mystic untapped to put equipment into play is critical to the game plan.

Failed to discard excess lands to pump Psychic Frog before combat damage. ESPN had 3 lands in hand (Polluted Delta, Watery Grave, Swamp) with 2 lands already in play. Discarding 1-2 lands to Psychic Frog would deal extra damage while still drawing a card from the combat damage trigger, effectively converting excess lands into damage.

Soul Spike can be cast for free by exiling two black cards from hand, dealing 4 damage and gaining 4 life. With two Soul Spikes and two Fatal Pushes in hand (all black cards), the player has the option to cast Soul Spike by exiling the other Soul Spike + a Fatal Push, providing a free 4-damage burst plus 4 life. Discarding a Soul Spike removes this powerful free-cast option. In a race situation against Hammer Time (which can threaten massive damage with Colossus Hammer + Leyline Axe), having access to a free 4-damage spell that also gains 4 life is extremely valuable. The player should have discarded a land instead (like Undercity Sewers which enters tapped, or one of the extra fetchlands/duals) since they already have two lands in play and multiple land drops in hand.

message: Select an artifact card with mana cost {0} or {1}
annotation_description: Missed lethal. Opponent's Psychic Frog and Emperor of Bones are both tapped, meaning no blockers. Player could use Stoneforge Mystic's ability to put Leyline Axe from hand onto the battlefield, then attack with Stoneforge Mystic and cast Battlefield Improvisation to attach Colossus Hammer + Leyline Axe (+ other equipment) to create a 15/16+ double strike trampler for 30+ unblockable damage against a 14hp opponent.

Missed lethal. With both opponent creatures tapped (no blockers), attacking Stoneforge Mystic and casting Battlefield Improvisation (1W available from Sacred Foundry + Sunbaked Canyon) would attach Colossus Hammer (+10/+10), Shadowspear (+1/+1, trample, lifelink), Leyline Axe (+1/+1, double strike, trample), and Paradise Mantle to the attacking Mystic. That makes it a 15/16 with double strike and trample, dealing 30 damage — more than enough to kill the opponent at 14 life.

Soul Spike can be cast for free by exiling two black cards from hand, dealing 4 damage and gaining 4 life. With the opponent at 9 life, Soul Spike represents a significant chunk of damage that could help close out the game. The player has Soul Spike in the graveyard already, plus this one in hand, and multiple black cards that could fuel the alternate cost. Discarding it removes a potential 4-damage burst that could be critical for finishing the opponent. While the mana cost of 7 is prohibitive, the alternate cost of exiling two black cards from hand is very achievable - the player has Fatal Push x2 and could draw more black cards. At 9 life, the opponent is in Soul Spike range if combined with Psychic Frog attacks.

Missed lethal. With both opponent creatures tapped and opponent at 11 life, casting Puresteel Paladin would activate Metalcraft (4 artifacts on board), allowing free equip of Colossus Hammer, Shadowspear, and Leyline Axe to Stoneforge Mystic for a massive double-striking, trampling, lifelinking attack that deals well over 11 damage unblocked.

Paid 2 life on Sacred Foundry to enter untapped (going from 8 to 6 life) against an aggressive board with Psychic Frog and Emperor of Bones. The player's reasoning was based on a hallucinated Puresteel Paladin on the battlefield, believing they could equip Colossus Hammer for free. Without Puresteel Paladin, the extra untapped mana is less critical, and preserving life at 8 rather than 6 would provide more buffer against the opponent's threats.

Playing Undercity Sewers (enters tapped) instead of Polluted Delta or Swamp delays casting Sheoldred, the Apocalypse by a full turn. With the opponent at 6 life, Sheoldred is devastating - it's a 4/5 deathtouch that drains the opponent whenever they draw. Additionally, cracking Polluted Delta would enable Revolt for Fatal Push to kill up to MV 4 creatures like Stoneforge Mystic.

Battlefield Improvisation provides lethal damage this turn. Stoneforge Mystic is attacking into no blockers. Casting Battlefield Improvisation (1W, payable with Plains + Sacred Foundry) gives +2/+2 and attaches all Equipment: Colossus Hammer (+10/+10), Shadowspear (+1/+1, trample, lifelink), Leyline Axe (+1/+1, double strike, trample), Paradise Mantle. That's 15 power with double strike and trample = 30 damage against 11 life. This is lethal.
